facts.statement: Fossils of Henodus chelyops have been found in Germany and Portugal.
facts.quote: Fossils of Henodus chelyops were found in the Estherienschichten Member of the Grabfeld Formation, near Tübingen, Germany and Loulé, Portugal.

facts.statement: Henodus lived during the Late Triassic period, specifically the early Carnian age.
facts.quote: Henodus (from , 'one' and , 'tooth') is an extinct placodont of the Late Triassic period during the early Carnian age.

facts.statement: Henodus was approximately 1 meter in length.
facts.quote: It was around 1 m in length.

facts.statement: Henodus is the only known placodont found in non-marine deposits, suggesting it lived in brackish or freshwater lagoons.
facts.quote: Henodus is the only placodont thus far found in non-marine deposits, suggesting it may have lived in brackish or freshwater lagoons.

facts.statement: Henodus possessed a shell consisting of a plastron on the underside and a carapace on top, similar to turtles.
facts.quote: Like turtles, it had a shell formed from a plastron on the underside and a carapace on top.

facts.statement: The carapace of Henodus extended beyond its limbs and was composed of bony scutes covered by horn plates.
facts.quote: The carapace extended well beyond the limbs, and was made up of individual plates of bony scutes covered by plates of horn.

facts.statement: Henodus's shell was made of many more bone pieces than a turtle's, forming a mosaic pattern.
facts.quote: However, the shell was composed of many more pieces of bone than that of turtles, forming a mosaic pattern.

facts.statement: Henodus's armor was fused to its spine, and its limbs were positioned normally, unlike turtles where limbs are inside the ribcage.
facts.quote: The armor was fused to its spine, and its limbs were situated in normal positions, unlike the turtle, where they are located inside the ribcage.

facts.statement: Henodus had weak limbs, suggesting it spent little to no time on land.
facts.quote: The weak limbs of Henodus suggest it spent little, if any time on land.

facts.statement: Henodus had baleen-like denticles and unique hyoid and musculature features indicating a filter-feeding lifestyle.
facts.quote: In addition, it had baleen-like denticles along the jaws, which combined with a unique feature of the hyoid and musculature indicative of rapid jaw closing indicate a filter feeding lifestyle.

facts.statement: Henodus was about 1 meter wide and had a flattened shell resembling a turtle due to convergent evolution.
facts.quote: Medía alrededor de 1 m de anchura, y producto de la evolución convergente, tenía el aspecto de una tortuga con el caparazón aplastado.

facts.statement: Henodus had wide and very strong jaws due to powerful muscles.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas del animal eran anchas y muy fuertes, gracias a la acción de poderosos músculos.

facts.statement: The palatal and lower jaw bones of Henodus provided great biting force.
facts.quote: Los huesos del paladar y las mandíbulas inferiores conferían una gran fuerza a la mordedura.

facts.statement: Henodus had short legs with webbed toes similar to ducks.
facts.quote: Las patas eran cortas, y sus dedos estaban unidas por una delicada membrana epitelial, a semejanza de los patos.

facts.statement: Henodus likely used its legs like flippers to improve swimming performance.
facts.quote: Probablemente, usaban las patas a modo de aletas para mejorar el rendimiento de la natación.

facts.statement: Henodus had a short, flat tail that moved side-to-side while swimming.
facts.quote: La cola era corta y plana, y se movía a los lados mientras nadaba.

facts.statement: It is believed Henodus could not retract its head under its shell like modern turtles.
facts.quote: Se cree que no tenía la facultad de retraer la cabeza bajo la concha como las tortugas actuales.

facts.statement: Henodus swam to the sea floor near the coast to find food.
facts.quote: Henodus nadaba hasta alcanzar el fondo marino cerca de la costa.

facts.statement: Henodus's preferred prey included clams, chitons, limpets, and oysters.
facts.quote: Allí se encontraban sus presas preferidas, seres como almejas, bígaros, lapas u ostras.

facts.statement: Henodus used its toothless horny beak to pull up prey and its molars to crush hard shells.
facts.quote: Una vez localizados, el animal los arrancaba con su pico córneo sin dientes, y trituraba las duras valvas con sus muelas.

facts.statement: The genus Henodus was described by Huene in 1936.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Huene, 1936

facts.statement: The family Henodontidae was established by von Huene in 1936.
facts.quote: familia_authority: von Huene, 1936

facts.statement: Henodus lived between 237 and 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

rejected.quote: Henodus also had a single tooth on each side of its mouth, though the remaining teeth were replaced by a beak.

rejected.quote: More recently, however, it has been suggested that this placodont was an aquatic herbivore, scraping off vegetation from the bottom with its broad jaws.
